evidence.excerpt:
While the Transformer architecture has become the de-facto standard for natural
language processing tasks, its applications to computer vision remain limited. In
vision, attention is either applied in conjunction with convolutional networks, or
used to replace certain components of convolutional networks while keeping their
overall structure in place. We show that this reliance on CNNs is not necessary
and a pure transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches can perform
very well on image classification tasks. When pre-trained on large amounts of
data and transferred to multiple mid-sized or small image recognition benchmarks
(ImageNet, CIFAR-100, VTAB, etc.), Vision Transformer (ViT) attains excellent
results compared to state-of-the-art convolutional networks while requiring sub-
stantially fewer computational resources to train.1

this, we remove the pre-trained prediction head and attach a zero-initialized D×K feedforward
layer, where K is the number of downstream classes. It is often beneficial to fine-tune at higher
resolution than pre-training (Touvron et al., 2019; Kolesnikov et al., 2020). When feeding images

evidence.excerpt:
Datasets. To explore model scalability, we use the ILSVRC-2012 ImageNet dataset with 1k classes
and 1.3M images (we refer to it as ImageNet in what follows), its superset ImageNet-21k with
21k classes and 14M images (Deng et al., 2009), and JFT (Sun et al., 2017) with 18k classes and
303M high-resolution images. We de-duplicate the pre-training datasets w.r.t. the test sets of the
downstream tasks following Kolesnikov et al. (2020). We transfer the models trained on these
dataset to several benchmark tasks: ImageNet on the original validation labels and the cleaned-up
ReaL labels (Beyer et al., 2020), CIFAR-10/100 (Krizhevsky, 2009), Oxford-IIIT Pets (Parkhi et al.,
2012), and Oxford Flowers-102 (Nilsback & Zisserman, 2008). For these datasets, pre-processing
follows Kolesnikov et al. (2020).

evidence.excerpt:
few-shot or fine-tuning accuracy.
Fine-tuning accuracies capture the performance of each model after fine-tuning it on the respective
dataset. Few-shot accuracies are obtained by solving a regularized least-squares regression problem
that maps the (frozen) representation of a subset of training images to{−1, 1}K target vectors. This
formulation allows us to recover the exact solution in closed form. Though we mainly focus on
fine-tuning performance, we sometimes use linear few-shot accuracies for fast on-the-fly evaluation
where fine-tuning would be too costly.

performs supervised transfer learning with large ResNets. The second is Noisy Student (Xie et al.,

achieved during training. To save compute, we report few-shot linear accuracy instead of full fine-
tuning accuracy. Figure 4 contains the results. Vision Transformers overfit more than ResNets with
comparable computational cost on smaller datasets. For example, ViT-B/32 is slightly faster than
ResNet50; it performs much worse on the 9M subset, but better on 90M+ subsets. The same is true
for ResNet152x2 and ViT-L/16. This result reinforces the intuition that the convolutional inductive
bias is useful for smaller datasets, but for larger ones, learning the relevant patterns directly from
data is sufficient, even beneficial.
Overall, the few-shot results on ImageNet (Figure 4), as well as the low-data results on VTAB
(Table 2) seem promising for very low-data transfer. Further analysis of few-shot properties of ViT
is an exciting direction of future work.

computational costs). Detailed results per model are provided in Table 6 in the Ap-
pendix. A few patterns can be observed. First, Vision Transformers dominate ResNets on the
performance/compute trade-off. ViT uses approximately 2− 4× less compute to attain the same
performance (average over 5 datasets). Second, hybrids slightly outperform ViT at small compu-
tational budgets, but the difference vanishes for larger models. This result is somewhat surprising,
since one might expect convolutional local feature processing to assist ViT at any size. Third, Vision
Transformers appear not to saturate within the range tried, motivating future scaling efforts.

evidence.excerpt:
We have explored the direct application of Transformers to image recognition. Unlike prior works
using self-attention in computer vision, we do not introduce image-specific inductive biases into
the architecture apart from the initial patch extraction step. Instead, we interpret an image as a
sequence of patches and process it by a standard Transformer encoder as used in NLP. This simple,
yet scalable, strategy works surprisingly well when coupled with pre-training on large datasets.
Thus, Vision Transformer matches or exceeds the state of the art on many image classification
datasets, whilst being relatively cheap to pre-train.
While these initial results are encouraging, many challenges remain. One is to apply ViT to other
computer vision tasks, such as detection and segmentation. Our results, coupled with those in Carion
et al. (2020), indicate the promise of this approach. Another

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes are measured on established external benchmark test splits and suites, including ImageNet ReaL, CIFAR-10/100, and the 19-task VTAB suite, which are decoupled from the pre-training datasets and provide independent ground-truth labels [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0023, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0030].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Top-1 accuracy on standard held-out validation and test sets (ImageNet, ImageNet ReaL, CIFAR-10/100, Oxford-IIIT Pets, Oxford Flowers-102, VTAB-1k) [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0027, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0030].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised cross-entropy loss on pre-training classification datasets (ImageNet, ImageNet-21k, JFT-300M) and fine-tuning target sets, optimized via Adam and SGD [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0023, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0026].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported experimental numbers directly support the claim that large-scale pre-training compensates for ViT's lack of translation equivariance and locality biases [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0007, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0034, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0037]. The paper also transparently shows that ViT underperforms comparable ResNets when trained from scratch on smaller datasets without large-scale pre-training [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0007, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0034].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation spans multiple standard benchmarks (ImageNet, ImageNet ReaL, CIFAR-10/100, Oxford-IIIT Pets, Oxford Flowers-102, and the 19-task VTAB suite), providing clear comparisons with leading CNN models like BiT and Noisy Student [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0023, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0029, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0030]. The authors include extensive scaling studies, ablations on architecture shapes, and compute-vs-accuracy trade-offs [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0037, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0039, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0040].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations are performed across established external ground-truth benchmark test splits and suites (including ReaL, CIFAR-10/100, and VTAB) that were decoupled from the pre-training datasets [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0023, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0030].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Top-1 accuracy on standard held-out validation and test sets (ImageNet, CIFAR-100, VTAB-1k, etc.) [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0027, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0030].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised cross-entropy loss on pre-training classification datasets (ImageNet, ImageNet-21k, JFT-300M) and fine-tuning target sets, optimized via Adam and SGD [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0023, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0026].

primary.limitations: The manuscript notes that ViT requires massive datasets to overcome the lack of inductive biases, that self-supervised ViT still trails supervised performance, and that extensions to dense prediction tasks like object detection and segmentation remain future work [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0007, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0048]. Furthermore, pre-training on proprietary data (JFT-300M) limits full external reproducibility, though models pre-trained on public ImageNet-21k are also provided [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0008, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0030].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly defined: images are divided into patches, flattened, linearly embedded, augmented with 1D learnable position embeddings and an extra class token, and processed using standard Transformer encoder layers [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0016, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0017]. The adaptation protocol for fine-tuning at higher resolutions using 2D positional embedding interpolation is precisely explained [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0020].
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a foundational, highly impactful paradigm shift in computer vision with comprehensive empirical rigor, well-scoped claims, transparent discussion of limitations on smaller datasets, and thorough baseline comparisons.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces the Vision Transformer (ViT), adapting a standard NLP Transformer architecture directly to sequences of flattened image patches for image classification without relying on convolutional layers [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0004, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0016]. It demonstrates that when pre-trained on sufficiently large datasets (such as ImageNet-21k or JFT-300M), ViT matches or exceeds state-of-the-art CNNs with lower pre-training computational cost [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0008, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0029, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0030].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides a foundational, highly impactful paradigm shift in computer vision with comprehensive empirical rigor, well-scoped claims, transparent discussion of limitations on smaller datasets, and thorough baseline comparisons.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The manuscript notes that ViT requires massive datasets to overcome the lack of inductive biases, that self-supervised ViT still trails supervised performance, and that extensions to dense prediction tasks like object detection and segmentation remain future work [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0007, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0048]. Furthermore, pre-training on proprietary data (JFT-300M) limits full external reproducibility, though models pre-trained on public ImageNet-21k are also provided [E50b19ad2797351eb-B0008, E50b19ad2797351eb-B0030].

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
